title: Particle MCMC: PMMH and particle Gibbs

items.title: Particle marginal Metropolis–Hastings
items.statement:
Fix observations $y_{1:T}$, a standard-Borel parameter space $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$,
a prior probability $\pi_0$, and the finite-horizon Feynman–Kac path model in
[[def-feynman-kac-path-targets-and-normalizers]]. Write
$$L_\theta(y_{1:T})=\gamma_{\theta,T}(1),\qquad C=\int_\Theta L_\theta(y_{1:T})\,\pi_0(d\theta).$$
Require every prefix normalizer $0<Z_{\theta,t}<\infty$ for $t=0,\ldots,T$
and $\pi_0$-almost every $\theta$, together with $0<C<\infty$; then the
parameter posterior is
$$\pi_y(d\theta)=C^{-1}L_\theta(y_{1:T})\,\pi_0(d\theta).$$

For fixed particle count $N\ge1$, let $U$ contain the full output of
[[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]] at $\theta$ and a terminal index
$K\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$ drawn conditionally with its final normalized weight.
Let $m_\theta(du)$ be this measurable auxiliary-variable probability kernel and
let $\widehat L_\theta(U)=\widehat Z_T$ be jointly measurable and nonnegative
in $(\theta,U)$. The required interface is
$$\int\widehat L_\theta(u)\,m_\theta(du)=L_\theta(y_{1:T});$$
[[thm-sequential-particle-estimator-is-unbiased]] supplies this identity under
its finite-horizon support and integrability hypotheses. Define the extended
target probability by
$$\widetilde\pi(d\theta,du)=C^{-1}\pi_0(d\theta)m_\theta(du)\widehat L_\theta(u).$$

Given current $(\theta,U)$, propose $\theta'\sim R(\theta,\cdot)$ and then
$U'\sim m_{\theta'}$. Apply the general Metropolis–Hastings construction
[[alg-metropolis-hastings-kernel]] to this proposal kernel and target
$\widetilde\pi$. On rejection retain the entire current pair $(\theta,U)$,
including its stored likelihood estimate and selected path index. When $\pi_0$
and $R$ have densities $p_0$ and $r$, and the current extended target density
is positive, the acceptance probability is
$$1\wedge\frac{p_0(\theta')\widehat L_{\theta'}(U')r(\theta\mid\theta')}{p_0(\theta)\widehat L_\theta(U)r(\theta'\mid\theta)}.$$
Initialize on the extended-target support, where $\pi_0(\theta)>0$ and
$\widehat L_\theta(U)>0$. Proposed zero estimates are rejected. A density-free version uses the
accepted-flow Radon–Nikodym construction in the cited general-state algorithm.

The selected path stored in $U$ is part of the auxiliary state. Refreshing its
estimate after rejection defines the different Monte Carlo within Metropolis
procedure, not this algorithm.

items.title: PMMH preserves the exact parameter posterior
items.statement:
Under the hypotheses of [[alg-pmmh]], assume the unbiasedness identity there
holds and the evidence $C$ is finite and positive. Then $\widetilde\pi$ is a
probability measure whose parameter marginal is $\pi_y$. With the terminal
index included in $U$, the joint marginal of $(\theta,X_{0:T}^{K})$ is the
posterior $C^{-1}\pi_0(d\theta)\gamma_{\theta,T}(dx_{0:T})$. The PMMH
transition kernel is reversible, hence invariant, for $\widetilde\pi$; its
parameter and selected-path marginals are therefore exact for every fixed
$N\ge1$. This is an invariance result only; it asserts no irreducibility,
uniqueness, convergence rate, or mixing speed.

items.title: Monte Carlo within Metropolis
items.statement:
Assume the parameter and likelihood-estimator inputs of [[alg-pmmh]], with
strictly positive estimates whenever the ratio is evaluated. At each iteration,
from the current parameter $\theta$, draw a fresh $U\sim m_\theta$; propose
$\theta'\sim R(\theta,\cdot)$ and independently draw $U'\sim m_{\theta'}$;
accept $\theta'$ with the same displayed ratio as [[alg-pmmh]], using the fresh
current estimate $\widehat L_\theta(U)$. Whether the proposal is accepted or
rejected, discard both auxiliary values before the next iteration and draw a
new estimate at the current parameter. The output state is $\theta$ only.

This is Monte Carlo within Metropolis (MCWM). It does not retain a single
extended state on rejection, so the pseudo-marginal invariance proof does not
apply. This definition makes no exactness or stationarity claim.

items.title: Particle Gibbs extended target
items.statement:
Use the finite-horizon state path model and proposal support conditions in
[[def-feynman-kac-path-targets-and-normalizers]],
[[thm-feynman-kac-path-radon-nikodym-weight]], and
[[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]]. Select the multinomial resampling branch, returning ancestor indices in sampled order. Residual resampling is not the labeled particle law used by this genealogical construction. Let $\pi_0$ be a proper parameter
prior, $\gamma_{\theta,T}$ the Feynman–Kac path measure at parameter $\theta$,
$L_\theta=\gamma_{\theta,T}(1)$, with $0<L_\theta<\infty$ for
$\pi_0$-almost every $\theta$, and
$$C=\int L_\theta\,\pi_0(d\theta),\qquad 0<C<\infty.$$
For a fixed particle count $N\ge2$, write
$$U=(X_0^{1:N},A_1^{1:N},X_1^{1:N},\ldots,A_T^{1:N},X_T^{1:N})$$
for the full particle system and ancestor indices generated by
[[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]]. Its forward probability law at
parameter $\theta$ is $\psi_\theta(du)$. The algorithm defines the product
normalizer estimate $\widehat Z_T(U)$ and final normalized weights
$W_T^1(U),\ldots,W_T^N(U)$; $K$ is a terminal particle index. The path
$X_{0:T}^{K}$ means the states on the ancestral lineage of particle $K$,
traced through the arrays $A_1^{1:N},\ldots,A_T^{1:N}$.

More explicitly, relative to counting measure on ancestor arrays and the
ordered SIR proposal-kernel integrals for the states,
$$\psi_\theta(du)=\prod_{i=1}^N\nu_{\theta,0}(dx_0^i)\prod_{t=1}^T\prod_{i=1}^N\left[W_{t-1}^{A_t^i}(U)R_{\theta,t}(X_{t-1}^{A_t^i},dx_t^i)\right].$$
Each factor $W_{t-1}^{A_t^i}(U)$ is the categorical mass of that ancestor
choice; no state transition density is assumed for the genealogical variant.

The genealogical particle Gibbs extended target is the measure
$$\varphi_N(d\theta,du,k)=C^{-1}\pi_0(d\theta)\,\psi_\theta(du)\,\widehat Z_T(u)W_T^k(u),\qquad k\in\{1,\ldots,N\}.$$
The selected state is $(\theta,X_{0:T}^{K})$. The zero-weight fallback in the
particle algorithm defines $W_T$ everywhere; when $\widehat Z_T=0$ the extended
target assigns the configuration zero mass.

The measure is a probability and has the exact joint smoothing posterior as
its selected $(\theta,X_{0:T}^{K})$ marginal by
[[thm-particle-gibbs-selected-path-marginal]].

items.title: Conditional particle filter for particle Gibbs
items.statement:
Fix $N\ge2$, a finite horizon $T$, a parameter $\theta$, and a reference
trajectory $x^*_{0:T}$ with a reference lineage of particle indices
$b_0,\ldots,b_T\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$. Use the proposal kernels, incremental
weights, and normalized resampling weights of
[[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]]. Use multinomial resampling with indices in sampled order. Require target-path domination as in [[thm-feynman-kac-path-radon-nikodym-weight]] and a retained $(\theta,x^*,b)$ in the measurable full-measure good set $D$ of [[def-particle-gibbs-extended-target]]. The formulas are conditional-law versions for posterior-almost every reference path; membership in topological support alone is insufficient. Outside $D$, return status “unavailable” and leave the retained parameter-path-lineage state unchanged in the sweep. If an arithmetic operation in a sampled particle system is undefined or a required normalizing sum is zero/nonfinite, also return “unavailable” and retain the old state; on $D$ these events have conditional probability zero by the factorization theorem.

1. Draw the $N-1$ initial particles other than $X_0^{b_0}$ independently from
   $\nu_0$, and set $X_0^{b_0}=x_0^*$.
2. For $t=1,\ldots,T$, for every $i\ne b_t$ draw an ancestor $A_t^i$ from the
   categorical distribution with probabilities $W_{t-1}^{1:N}$ and then draw
   $X_t^i$ from the proposal kernel conditional on $X_{t-1}^{A_t^i}$. Set
   $A_t^{b_t}=b_{t-1}$ and $X_t^{b_t}=x_t^*$. Compute all incremental and
   normalized weights by the SIR rule.
3. Return the conditional particle system, its weights, and ancestry arrays.

In a particle Gibbs sweep, the conditional particle filter is followed by a
draw $K\sim\mathrm{Categorical}(W_T^{1:N})$ and tracing the ancestry of $K$.
For a joint parameter-path target, first update $\theta$ from its exact full
conditional given the retained path. This procedure defines the finite
conditional particle Gibbs update; its correctness is a separate result.

items.title: The particle Gibbs extended target has the exact smoothing marginal
items.statement:
Assume the hypotheses of [[def-particle-gibbs-extended-target]] and
[[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]], with multinomial resampling in sampled order, including the finite-horizon support
conditions and $0<L_\theta<\infty$ for prior-almost every $\theta$, with
$0<C=\int L_\theta\,\pi_0(d\theta)<\infty$. Then $\varphi_N$ in
[[def-particle-gibbs-extended-target]] is a probability measure and its
selected $(\theta,X_{0:T}^{K})$ marginal is
$$C^{-1}\pi_0(d\theta)\gamma_{\theta,T}(dx_{0:T}),$$
the exact joint parameter and smoothing posterior, for every $N\ge2$.

items.title: The conditional particle Gibbs sweep is a Gibbs update
items.statement:
Under [[def-particle-gibbs-extended-target]] and
[[alg-conditional-particle-gibbs]], for $\varphi_N$-almost every extended
state the conditional law of the terminal index $K$ given the particle cloud
is $\mathrm{Categorical}(W_T^{1:N})$. For posterior-almost every retained parameter-trajectory-lineage value, the remaining particles and
ancestor indices have exactly the conditional-particle-filter law in
[[alg-conditional-particle-gibbs]]. The parameter conditional is the ordinary
posterior full conditional given the selected path. Consequently these are
Gibbs updates of the extended target. The measurable exceptional-state identity fallback specified by the algorithm is included. Their composition leaves that target
invariant and has the exact joint parameter-path posterior as its selected
marginal. This invariance does not assert fast mixing.

items.title: Backward-simulation particle Gibbs extended target
items.statement:
Assume the finite-horizon Feynman–Kac model and proposal support conditions in
[[def-feynman-kac-path-targets-and-normalizers]] and
[[thm-feynman-kac-path-radon-nikodym-weight]]. Use the multinomial SIR law with ancestor indices in sampled order. Residual resampling is not included in this labeled-density construction. For this variant, additionally
assume that the initial target law has a measurable density $\mu_{\theta,0}$,
each target transition $M_{\theta,t}$ has a jointly measurable density
$f_{\theta,t}(x_t\mid x_{t-1})$, and each proposal transition $R_{\theta,t}$ has
a density $q_{\theta,t}(x_t\mid x_{t-1})$, all with respect to declared
sigma-finite coordinate reference measures. Let $q_{\theta,0}$ be the proposal
initial density with respect to the initial coordinate reference measure.
Retain the proper-prior and positive-finite-evidence assumptions of
[[def-particle-gibbs-extended-target]]. Then
the path measure has density
$$\gamma_{\theta,T}(x_{0:T})=\mu_{\theta,0}(x_0)G_0(x_0)\prod_{t=1}^Tf_{\theta,t}(x_t\mid x_{t-1})G_t(x_t).$$
Require positive finite denominators in the backward probabilities below on
the extended-target support.

Write $U$ for all SIR particles and ancestor indices, $\psi_\theta(u)$ for
their forward joint density, and $j=(j_0,\ldots,j_T)$ for a sequence of
particle indices. Let $x^j_{0:T}$ be the path formed from states
$X_t^{j_t}$, without requiring $A_t^{j_t}=j_{t-1}$. For
$t=0,\ldots,T-1$, define
$$B_t^i(z;U)=\frac{W_t^i f_{\theta,t+1}(z\mid X_t^i)}{\sum_{\ell=1}^NW_t^\ell f_{\theta,t+1}(z\mid X_t^\ell)}.$$
The backward-simulation extended target is
$$\varphi_N^{\rm BS}(d\theta,du,j)=\frac{\pi_0(d\theta)\,\gamma_{\theta,T}(x^j_{0:T})}{C\,N^{T+1}}\frac{\psi_\theta(u)}{q_{\theta,0}(X_0^{j_0})\prod_{t=1}^TW_{t-1}^{A_t^{j_t}}q_{\theta,t}(X_t^{j_t}\mid X_{t-1}^{A_t^{j_t}})}\prod_{t=1}^TB_{t-1}^{A_t^{j_t}}(X_t^{j_t};U).$$
where the displayed expression is a density with respect to the common
particle reference measures, counting measure on ancestor and selected indices,
and the prior measure on $\theta$. The complete SIR forward density
$\psi_\theta$ includes the normalized ancestor probabilities and proposal
densities for every particle. This is the backward-simulation extension of the
particle Gibbs target; its exact selected-path marginal and Gibbs conditionals
are proved in
[[thm-particle-gibbs-backward-simulation-sweep-is-gibbs]].

items.title: Particle Gibbs with backward simulation
items.statement:
Use the density, support, and positive-denominator hypotheses of
[[def-particle-gibbs-backward-simulation-extended-target]]. Select multinomial resampling with ancestor indices in sampled order. Fix $N\ge2$. Before updating, require the retained state to be in $D_{\rm BS}$ of [[def-particle-gibbs-backward-simulation-extended-target]]; otherwise return the unchanged retained state. If a required ratio or normalizing sum is undefined, zero or nonfinite during a sweep, return the old retained state. The factorization theorem proves that such failures have conditional probability zero on the designated full-measure set. A
backward-simulation sweep on $(\theta,x^*,j)$ consists of the following
updates:

1. Draw $\theta'$ from the exact posterior full conditional given $x^*$ and
   the observations.
2. Run a conditional auxiliary particle filter at $\theta'$, conditioned on
   the reference trajectory $x^*$ and index sequence $j$. Initialize all
   particles except the indexed reference particle from the proposal. At each
   later time, draw each non-reference ancestor from the current normalized
   weights and propagate it with the proposal; fix the indexed reference state
   to its reference value and draw its ancestor $A_t^{j_t}$ with probabilities
   $B_{t-1}^i(x_t^{j_t};U)$.
3. Given the resulting particle cloud, draw $J_T$ from the final normalized
   weights $W_T^{1:N}$. For $t=T-1,T-2,\ldots,0$, draw
   $J_t$ with probabilities $B_t^{1:N}(X_{t+1}^{J_{t+1}};U)$. Return
   $\theta'$ and the selected path $X_0^{J_0},\ldots,X_T^{J_T}$ together with
   the new index sequence.

The conditional auxiliary particle filter and the backward simulator are the
two particle-coordinate conditionals of
[[def-particle-gibbs-backward-simulation-extended-target]]. Their Gibbs
interpretation and exact posterior marginal are separate proved properties.

items.title: The backward-simulation sweep is a Gibbs update
items.statement:
Under [[def-particle-gibbs-backward-simulation-extended-target]] and
[[alg-particle-gibbs-backward-simulation]], for posterior-almost every retained state in the stated good set, the conditional law of the
remaining particle system given $(\theta,x^*,j)$ is the stated conditional
auxiliary particle filter, and the conditional law of the index sequence given
the particle system is the backward simulator with terminal weights $W_T$ and
backward probabilities $B_t$. The extended target is a probability measure
whose selected $(\theta,x^*)$ marginal is the exact joint smoothing posterior.
With the measurable identity fallback on exceptional retained states, each sweep step agrees almost everywhere with a Gibbs update, so the extended target is invariant for
every fixed $N\ge2$. No fast-mixing or ergodicity claim follows.

title: Particle MCMC: PMMH and particle Gibbs — Examples

items.title: Pseudo-marginal rejection retains the current likelihood estimate
items.statement:
Let $\Theta=\{0,1\}$ with uniform prior, exact likelihoods $L_0=L_1=1$, and
a symmetric proposal that flips the parameter. At $\theta=0$ let the unbiased
likelihood estimator be $\widehat L_0=1$ surely. At $\theta=1$ let
$\widehat L_1=1/2$ or $3/2$, each with probability $1/2$. The pseudo-marginal
target on parameter and estimate has masses
$$\widetilde\pi(0,1)=1/2,\qquad \widetilde\pi(1,1/2)=1/8,\qquad \widetilde\pi(1,3/2)=3/8.$$
The parameter marginal is uniform, although the estimate conditional on
$\theta=1$ is size-biased. A rejection at $(1,3/2)$ retains $3/2$ for the next
ratio calculation.

items.title: Refreshing the current estimate can destroy exactness
items.statement:
Replacing an exact likelihood by an unbiased estimate freshly drawn at both the
current and proposed parameter in every Metropolis step necessarily leaves the
exact parameter posterior invariant.

items.title: An invariant particle Gibbs chain can be sticky
items.statement:
Take the one-time model $T=0$ with state space $\{0,1\}$, target
$\pi(0)=99/100$, $\pi(1)=1/100$, and proposal
$q(0)=1/100$, $q(1)=99/100$. Both target states are in proposal support. Use
$N=2$ particles: one is the retained reference state, the other is sampled
from $q$, and the next state is drawn from the two importance weights
$w(x)=\pi(x)/q(x)$. This is the one-time conditional particle Gibbs update.

items.title: A particle Gibbs proposal that misses posterior path support
items.statement:
A particle Gibbs exactness construction remains well-defined with its usual
finite importance weights even if its proposal assigns zero probability to a
positive-mass posterior path.
